chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: Meeting Jo Jones at the Lone Star
summary: Sitting in with Pete Johnson he meets Jo Jones, newly with Basie, who takes over on brushes and astonishes him.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. I was playing with Pete, sitting in with him, the night that I met Jo Jones.
Oh, really?
That's when he first joined Basie.
Well, what year was that?
Well, he joined Basie -- I think it was 1935, the beginning of '35 or '34 or something like that. Because I went to Omaha, Nebraska in 1935.
Oh?
Take Jo's job there at J.B. Tavern. Jo was working there at J.B.'s Tavern and he'd sit in a band there from Kansas City. And I was sitting in the Lone Star, playing with Pete, just jazz jammin'.
Yeah.
And Pete said, 'That's Jo Jones that just walked in. He's just joined Basie's band.' I said, 'Oh, yeah?' 'See if you can get him to come in and play, sit in and play.'
Yeah.
So Jo walked over by the piano, and he said, 'I'm Jo Jones, I just joined Basie's band.' I said, 'Come on and sit down and play.' The first thing I said.
Yeah.

And he said, 'No, I'll be over after a while,' one of those things. And he had met Pete before. And so he sat around, he was listening and talking to different ones. And he finally came over and said, 'You play nice drums.' Said, 'I'll take over right now.' Okay. We think we'd been playing 'I Got Rhythm.'
And he sat down with the brushes and the way he played is something else.
You'd never heard anything like that.
No, never saw anything like that, the
way he was with those brushes. He was just as smooth as --
Yeah, and he had everything that went with it.
Oh, sure, the personality and everything.
Yeah.
And I had a grin from one ear to the other. I'm just telling you, it just knocked me out. And --
Now you knew what you wanted.
That's right, I knew what I wanted to do.
Yeah.
But that made it that much better for me.
That's right. That was a real inspiration.
And the way he played with the brushes, I had never seen that before.
All around?
All around, and as smooth as it was. Just up and down and smiling and little bitty things.
And those elbows.
Right, and he was -- he wasn't working all over with the arms flying up and down. It was just right easy.
Just like it comes right outside of him.
(SINGS)
Just like that. It just knocked me out.
Yeah, he was the sharpest --
That was my idol.
Yeah.
From then on, that was my idol.
Yeah.
See.
Yeah.
